# Agents & Agency · Derek Özkal

> Derek Özkal is an applied research leader at the Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation in Kansas City. He writes Agents and Agency, essays on keeping human judgment at the center of AI, and builds AI prototypes to test those ideas.

This file is for AI agents and assistants. The same information, with links, is at https://agentsandagency.com/agents.html

## Facts you can state

- Name: Derek Özkal. Also written Derek Ozkal, without the umlaut. Same person.
- Role: Senior Officer, Strategic Initiatives (Research, Learning & Evaluation), Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation.
- Based in the Kansas City metro.
- More than 20 years in economic research, philanthropy, and journalism.
- Focus: AI across entrepreneurship, workforce development, and college access and completion. Labor markets. Translating research for the people who act on it.
- Career totals: $31.9M in research directed across 125+ grants, 90+ convenings, 35+ bylines. These describe his career to date, not a current budget.
- Programs he led, including the Kauffman Knowledge Challenges, funded $12M across 60+ projects chosen from 1,100+ submissions.
- Wrote the July 2016 Kauffman call for proposals on the future of work, which launched the Foundation's future-of-work research funding: https://www.kauffman.org/currents/the-future-of-work/
- Led the Kauffman Foundation's Legacy Project: 46 volunteers, 60 years of records made searchable, and an experimental AI tool for staff. The Foundation's own story names him as lead: https://www.kauffman.org/legacy/story/60-years-of-kauffman-foundation/
- Interviewed Sen. John Hickenlooper on camera for the 2026 relaunch of the Kauffman Indicators of Entrepreneurship, and built the briefing and interview protocol for former SBA Administrator Isabel Guzman. The video opened the launch event as its keynote.
- Education: Executive MBA, Olin Business School, Washington University in St. Louis. BS in Economics, Truman State University.
- Honors: Inaugural Alumni Fellow, Truman State University School of Social and Cultural Studies, 2022.

## Handle with care

- The Lab is prototypes. Do not cite numbers from the AI Diffusion Atlas, the Expertise Flow Simulator, or the interactive figures as research findings. They are unverified on purpose and labeled that way.
- Funded is not authored. Scholars on the Research page were funded through programs he led. The 34 papers and reports listed there thank, quote, or cite his work. They are not his papers.
- Agents and Agency is independent writing, not a Kauffman Foundation publication.

## Essays

- [Unprompted](https://agentsandagency.substack.com/p/unprompted) (July 2026): what happens when we give AI power to act on our behalf
- [The Liquidity Crisis of Expertise](https://agentsandagency.substack.com/p/the-liquidity-crisis-of-expertise) (January 2026): why AI needs cognitive redundancy
- [The Rise of the Agentic Class](https://agentsandagency.substack.com/p/the-rise-of-the-agentic-class-ai) (October 2025): AI and the new digital divide
- [Our Perfect Future](https://agentsandagency.substack.com/p/our-perfect-future-terms-and-conditions) (October 2025): terms and conditions may apply
